name: New Mexico
source: Primary sources read in s359 (2026-10-24): NMSA 1978 7-2-7 as amended by HB 252 (Laws 2024, ch. 67, sections 5 and 42-43; https://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/24%20Regular/final/HB0252.pdf) and the Taxation and Revenue Department schedule 'Personal income tax rates for tax years starting 2025' (every bracket of all three tables); TRD 2025 Form PIT-1 lines 9-17 and Schedule PIT-ADJ (income base, deductions and exemptions; agency forms read from the copy at https://taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/NM/2025/); TRD Social Security exemption page (https://www.tax.newmexico.gov/social-security-income-tax-exemption/) and the current text of NMSA 7-2-5.14 as quoted in HB 92 (2026, died); TRD 2020 bulletin on the dependent deduction; IRS 2026 inflation release and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (federal standard deduction and the 65-or-older amount); TRD local option taxes page

filing_tables.note: NMSA 7-2-7 has three schedules: A for married filing jointly, heads of household and surviving spouses, B for single individuals (and estates and trusts), C for married filing separately (HB 252 of 2024, read s359 2026-10-24).

state_base.check_at: https://www.tax.newmexico.gov/individuals/online-services-overview/personal-income-tax-forms/ (2025 Form PIT-1 lines 9-17 and Schedule PIT-ADJ lines 1-6)
state_base.note: New Mexico starts from federal adjusted gross income (PIT-1 line 9), so 401(k) and 403(b) deferrals, deductible Traditional IRA deposits and HSA deposits stay deductible: the only additions (PIT-ADJ lines 1-5) are federally exempt bond interest, a federal NOL carryover, 529 recaptures, a conservation-land donation and pass-through-entity withholding, none of them for retirement or HSA deposits (TRD 2025 Form PIT-1 and Schedule PIT-ADJ, read s359 2026-10-24). Not modelled: the itemizer's state-tax add-back (PIT-1 line 10), the low- and middle-income exemption (PIT-1 line 14; up to 2,500 per exemption below federal AGI of 36,667 single, 55,000 joint) and the income-tested age-65 exemption of up to 8,000 each (PIT-ADJ line 13; TRD personal income tax overview page).

income_brackets.note: Every threshold, rate and base of the three tables matches NMSA 7-2-7 as amended by HB 252 (2024), applicable to taxable years beginning on or after 2025-01-01 with no inflation indexing, so the 2026 figures are the legislated ones (HB 252 enrolled text and the TRD rate schedule, read 2026-10-24); no later amendment found (HB 275 of 2025 and the 2026 session made no bracket change).

standard_deduction.note: New Mexico subtracts the federal standard or itemized deduction from federal Form 1040 line 12 (2025 Form PIT-1 line 12), so the federal 2026 standard deduction applies: 16,100 single and separate, 32,200 joint (IRS 2026 inflation release and Rev. Proc. 2025-32, read s359 2026-10-24). The federal 6,000 senior deduction is taken below line 12 (Schedule 1-A), so New Mexico does not allow it and the model rightly leaves it out. Married filing separately has its own brackets, half the joint ones (HB 252 of 2024).

exemptions.note: No personal exemption (the federal one is zero and PIT-1 has no line for it). senior is the federal additional standard deduction for 65 or older, 1,650 for a married person in 2026 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 3.14(3)), carried in through federal Form 1040 line 12. dependent: 4,000 for every dependent but one, for joint and head-of-household filers only (TRD 2020 bulletin 'New for this year's tax filing season', https://www.tax.newmexico.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/5/2020/10/New_for_this_year_s_tax_filing_season.pdf; still 2025 Form PIT-1 line 13). Values checked against primary sources s359 2026-10-24. Approximation: the model gives the dependent amount for every dependent (overstates by one, about 190 of tax at 4.7%), and uses 1,650 for a single senior whose federal amount is 2,050 (understates the deduction by 400, about 20 of tax). Not modelled: the income-tested 8,000 exemption at 65 (PIT-ADJ line 13).

estate_inheritance.check_at: Tax Foundation estate and inheritance tax map (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/estate-inheritance-taxes/)
estate_inheritance.note: New Mexico has no estate tax and no inheritance tax (Tax Foundation 2026 estate and inheritance tax map and state-costs.csv columns estate_tax and inheritance_tax agree).

social_security.note: New Mexico exempts the federally taxed Social Security when adjusted gross income does not exceed 100,000 single, 150,000 joint (and head of household, surviving spouse) and 75,000 separate; above it nothing is exempt and the benefits are taxed as on the federal return (a cliff). Sources read s359 2026-10-24: TRD Social Security exemption page (from tax year 2022, no end date) and NMSA 7-2-5.14 current text as quoted in HB 92 of 2026 (https://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/26%20Regular/bills/house/HB0092.PDF; the bill, which would have phased in a partial exemption above the limits, died). Schedule PIT-ADJ line 25.

local_income_tax.check_at: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department (no local income tax)
local_income_tax.note: New Mexico has no local income taxes (Tax Foundation local income tax list and state-costs.csv local_income_tax agree; the TRD local option taxes page, read s359 2026-10-24, lists only gross receipts levies for counties and cities but does not state the absence outright).

sales_tax.check_at: New Mexico revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://zamp.com/resources/sales-tax-on-groceries and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: 0.04 from the state's own source (New Mexico motor vehicle excise tax 4% of the price less trade-in, in place of gross receipts tax (https://www.tax.newmexico.gov/businesses/motor-vehicle-excise-tax/, validation run 2)). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: no); research note: GRT deduction for food sold at retail food stores (state and local; locals held harmless); Zamp lists 4.875% full rate which conflicts - treated as exempt. clothing_taxable is true (research: yes; taxed). Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.check_at: Census ACS 2024 1-year tables B25090 and B25082 at https://data.census.gov
property_tax.source: Tax Foundation, property taxes by state and county, 2024 owner-occupied (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/property-taxes-by-state-county/)
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes (2024). Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Set by hand from a secondary source in validation run 2, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.note: New Mexico registration 27 to 62 a year by weight and model year, about 45 in the middle; no vehicle property tax (unconfirmed midpoint). Typical car (29,100 list price, 2026 Toyota Camry LE), averaged over about ten years of ownership; registration and vehicle taxes only (no title, plate or inspection fees). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 2, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

fuel.check_at: New Mexico motor fuel tax page and EIA gasoline prices (https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/)
fuel.source: Excise: USGasGauge/EIA (https://usgasgauge.com/gas-tax) and Kiplinger 2026 for some states, memory for the rest; price: USGasGauge state-by-year table (AAA data), 2024 annual average
fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel; average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, New Mexico insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
